title: Hagia Sophia completed
summary: Justinian's great church, with a dome that seems to float on light, is consecrated. It remained the world's largest cathedral for nearly a thousand years.

title: Plague of Justinian
summary: The first recorded pandemic of bubonic plague sweeps the Mediterranean, killing perhaps a quarter of the population of Constantinople and crippling Justinian's reconquest of the West.

title: Code of Justinian
summary: Emperor Justinian has Roman law collected and systematised. The Corpus Juris Civilis is still the foundation of civil law in much of Europe and Latin America.

title: Lombards invade Italy
summary: The Lombards pour into Italy and conquer most of the peninsula, ending Justinian's short-lived reunification of Italy.

title: Sui dynasty reunites China
summary: After almost 300 years of division, the Sui conquer the south and reunite China. They build the Grand Canal linking the Yellow and Yangtze rivers.

title: The Hijra: Muhammad moves to Medina
summary: The Prophet Muhammad and his followers migrate from Mecca to Medina, where he founds the first Muslim community. The Islamic calendar counts years from this event.

title: Tang dynasty founded
summary: The Tang dynasty begins a golden age: Chang'an becomes the world's largest city, poetry flourishes (Li Bai, Du Fu) and Chinese culture spreads to Korea, Japan and Vietnam.

title: Battle of the Yarmouk
summary: Arab Muslim armies crush the Byzantines; Syria, Palestine and soon Egypt are lost to the Empire for good.

title: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
summary: The Rashidun Caliphate defeats the Sasanian Persians. Within 15 years the ancient Persian Empire is gone and Iran becomes part of the Islamic world.

title: Umayyad conquest of Hispania
summary: Tariq ibn Ziyad crosses the strait (giving Gibraltar its name, 'Jabal Tariq') and defeats the Visigoths. Most of Iberia becomes al-Andalus.

title: Battle of Tours
summary: Charles Martel's Franks defeat an Umayyad raiding army deep in Gaul, marking the high tide of Muslim expansion into Western Europe.

title: Abbasids overthrow the Umayyads
summary: The Abbasid revolution topples the Umayyad Caliphate. A surviving Umayyad prince escapes to found an emirate in Córdoba.

title: Battle of Talas
summary: The Abbasids defeat a Tang Chinese army, halting China's expansion westward. Legend says captured Chinese papermakers brought the craft to Samarkand.

title: An Lushan Rebellion
summary: A Tang general's rebellion devastates northern China; the death toll was enormous. The Tang survive but never fully recover their power.

title: Baghdad founded
summary: Caliph al-Mansur builds a round city on the Tigris as the Abbasid capital. Its House of Wisdom becomes a centre for translating Greek, Persian and Indian science.

title: Vikings raid Lindisfarne
summary: Norse raiders plunder the monastery of Lindisfarne, opening the Viking Age of raids, trade and settlement from North America to Baghdad.

title: Kyoto becomes Japan's capital
summary: Emperor Kanmu moves the capital to Heian-kyō, opening the Heian period of Japanese court culture that produced 'The Tale of Genji'.

title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
summary: Pope Leo III crowns the Frankish king Charlemagne 'Emperor of the Romans', reviving the imperial title in the West.

title: Treaty of Verdun
summary: Charlemagne's grandsons divide his empire into three kingdoms — the rough outlines of France, Germany and the lands in between.

title: Cyril and Methodius' mission to the Slavs
summary: Byzantine missionaries create the Glagolitic alphabet to translate scripture into Slavonic; their followers develop Cyrillic, used today from Bulgaria to Russia.

title: Kyivan Rus' founded
summary: Oleg of Novgorod takes Kyiv, uniting the Rus' lands along the trade route from the Baltic to Constantinople.

title: Classic Maya collapse
summary: The great southern Maya cities such as Tikal are abandoned over a century, probably due to drought, warfare and overpopulation. Chichén Itzá in the north rises.

title: Caliphate of Córdoba proclaimed
summary: Abd al-Rahman III declares himself caliph. Córdoba, with perhaps 100,000+ people, libraries and the Great Mosque, is the most sophisticated city in Western Europe.

title: Otto I crowned — Holy Roman Empire
summary: The German king Otto the Great is crowned emperor by the pope. The Holy Roman Empire lasts, in some form, until 1806.

title: Song dynasty founded
summary: Zhao Kuangyin founds the Song. Under it China invents movable type, the compass for navigation, gunpowder weapons and paper money, and its economy is the world's largest.

title: Fatimids found Cairo
summary: The Shia Fatimid dynasty conquers Egypt and founds al-Qāhira, 'the Victorious', with al-Azhar mosque and university.

title: Christianisation of Kyivan Rus'
summary: Grand Prince Vladimir accepts Orthodox Christianity from Byzantium and has the people of Kyiv baptised in the Dnieper.

title: Norse reach North America
summary: Leif Erikson and fellow Norse Greenlanders reach 'Vinland'. Their short-lived settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows is the first known European presence in the Americas.

title: The Tale of Genji
summary: Murasaki Shikibu, a lady at the Heian court, writes 'The Tale of Genji', often called the world's first novel.

title: East–West Schism
summary: Papal legates and the Patriarch of Constantinople excommunicate each other, formalising the split between the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

title: Battle of Hastings
summary: William of Normandy defeats and kills King Harold II. The Norman Conquest transforms England's ruling class, language and laws.

title: Battle of Manzikert
summary: The Seljuk Turks under Alp Arslan defeat and capture Byzantine Emperor Romanos IV. Turkish tribes pour into Anatolia — the beginning of Turkey.

title: Byzantine Golden Bull for Venice
summary: In return for naval help against the Normans, Emperor Alexios I grants Venetian merchants tax-free trade throughout the Byzantine Empire and their own quarter in Constantinople — the foundation of Venice's commercial empire.

title: Crusaders capture Jerusalem
summary: The First Crusade, called by Pope Urban II in 1095, takes Jerusalem and massacres its inhabitants. Crusader states are set up along the Levant coast, enriching the Italian maritime cities that supply them.

title: The Venetian Arsenal founded
summary: Venice founds its state shipyard. By the 1500s the Arsenal, using assembly-line methods, could turn out a galley a day and employed up to 16,000 people.

title: Angkor Wat completed
summary: King Suryavarman II's temple to Vishnu, the largest religious monument on Earth, is completed at the heart of the Khmer Empire's capital.

title: Kamakura shogunate established
summary: Minamoto no Yoritomo is named shogun. For nearly 700 years real power in Japan lies with military rulers, while emperors reign in Kyoto.

title: Battle of Hattin; Saladin takes Jerusalem
summary: Saladin destroys the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem and retakes the city that October, prompting the Third Crusade of Richard the Lionheart.

title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
summary: Unable to pay Venice for its fleet, the Fourth Crusade is diverted to Constantinople, which is stormed and looted.
significance: The Byzantine Empire is carved up between crusader lords and Venice; it is restored in 1261 but never recovers its strength.

title: Temüjin proclaimed Genghis Khan
summary: A kurultai of the steppe tribes proclaims Temüjin Genghis Khan. The Mongol Empire he founds becomes the largest contiguous land empire in history.

title: Magna Carta
summary: Rebel barons force King John to accept a charter limiting royal power and promising justice under law — later a symbol of constitutional government.

title: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
summary: The Christian kings of Castile, Aragon and Navarre defeat the Almohads, opening southern Spain to the Reconquista.

title: Sundiata founds the Mali Empire
summary: Sundiata Keita defeats the Sosso king Sumanguru at Kirina and founds the Mali Empire, which grows rich on West African gold.

title: Mongols invade Europe: Battle of Mohi
summary: Mongol armies destroy the Polish and Hungarian forces at Legnica and Mohi. They withdraw the next year when the Great Khan Ögedei dies.

title: Mongols sack Baghdad
summary: Hülegü Khan sacks Baghdad, kills the last Abbasid caliph and destroys the House of Wisdom — a catastrophe for the Islamic world.

title: Battle of Ain Jalut
summary: The Mamluks of Egypt defeat a Mongol army for the first time, halting the Mongol advance into Africa.

title: Byzantines retake Constantinople
summary: Michael VIII Palaiologos recaptures the city from the Latins with Genoese help — a blow to Venice, whose rival Genoa now gains Black Sea privileges.

title: Marco Polo travels to China
summary: Venetian merchant Marco Polo sets off with his father and uncle along the Silk Road and serves Kublai Khan for 17 years. His book of travels, dictated in a Genoese prison, fascinated Europe.

title: Kublai Khan founds the Yuan dynasty
summary: Kublai proclaims the Yuan dynasty and in 1279 completes the conquest of Song China — the first time all of China is ruled by foreign conquerors.

title: Mongol invasion of Japan wrecked by typhoon
summary: A huge Mongol-Korean-Chinese fleet is destroyed by a typhoon the Japanese called the kamikaze, 'divine wind'.

title: Great Zimbabwe at its height
summary: The Shona capital's massive dry-stone walls enclose a city of up to 18,000 people that grew rich trading gold and ivory to the Swahili coast.

title: Cahokia at its peak
summary: The Mississippian city of Cahokia, with the giant earthwork Monks Mound, may have held 10,000–20,000 people — larger than London at the time.

title: Chola raid on Srivijaya
summary: The south Indian Chola emperor Rajendra I launches a naval expedition that sacks the cities of Srivijaya, the maritime empire controlling the spice route.

title: University of Bologna founded
summary: Students in Bologna organise to study law, creating the oldest university in continuous operation; Paris and Oxford follow within a century.

title: Timbuktu becomes a trade centre
summary: Founded by Tuareg nomads, Timbuktu grows into a hub of the trans-Saharan trade in gold and salt and later a famous centre of Islamic scholarship.
